Feluda.description: Prodosh C. Mitter, known as Feluda, is a private investigator and the protagonist who uses the alias Mr Sengupta to inquire about suspects.

Uncle Sidhu.description: A knowledgeable family friend and polymath with a deep interest in Indian art who provides Feluda with vital information.

Srinath.description: A household helper who assists with chores such as making tea.

Saul Silverstein.description: Saul Silverstein is an American tourist and art collector who attempted to buy the stolen yakshi's head from the Raja-Rani temple.

Tintin.description: A famous European comic book series featuring the young reporter Tintin, popular among Indian readers.

Tintin in Tibet.description: A specific adventure from the Tintin comic series, set in the Himalayas.

Chariots of the Gods.description: A book by Erich von Däniken proposing that ancient civilizations were influenced by extraterrestrials.

pyramid of Giza.description: The Great Pyramid in Egypt, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

Nile.description: A major river in Egypt, historically significant for ancient civilizations.

Easter Island.description: A remote island in the South Pacific Ocean, famous for its large stone statues called moai.

Peru.description: A country in South America, known for ancient civilizations and mysterious geoglyphs like the Nazca Lines.

Mahabharata.description: An ancient Indian epic that describes the Kurukshetra War and contains mythological and historical narratives.

Kurukshetra.description: The battlefield described in the Mahabharata where a great war took place.

Qutab Minar.description: A historic minaret in Delhi, India, known for its iron pillar that has not rusted for centuries.

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, rich in historical monuments.

Bhubaneshwar.description: A city in the Indian state of Odisha, known for its ancient temples.

Raja-Rani temple.description: A famous temple in Bhubaneshwar, renowned for its architectural beauty and sculptures.

Grand Hotel.description: A hotel in Bhubaneshwar where the American tourist is staying.

Rajput.description: A member of a prominent warrior class in India, also known for their distinctive style of painting.

Varanasi.description: A holy city in India, known for its religious significance and art.

Nagarmal.description: A shop owner in the Grand Hotel arcade, known to Uncle Sidhu.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, mentioned as Saul Silverstein's next destination.

divan.description: A long, low sofa without a back or arms, often found in South Asian homes.

tonnes.description: A metric unit of mass equal to 1,000 kilograms, commonly used in India and many other countries.

chowkidar.description: A watchman or guard, typically employed to look after property.

yakshi.description: A yakshi is a female nature spirit from Indian mythology, often depicted in temple sculptures.

cheroot.description: A type of cigar with both ends cut flat, popular in South Asia.

Tantric.description: Relating to Tantra, a tradition of esoteric rituals and philosophies in Hinduism and Buddhism.

Topshe.description: Tapesh, known as Topshe, is Feluda's young cousin and the narrator of the stories who accompanies him on cases.

Balaram Ghosh.description: The taxi driver who drives Feluda and Topshe to Sidikpur and becomes curious about their mission.

Ali.description: A local boy from Sidikpur who helps Feluda by pointing out another boy who found the statue's head.

Panu.description: A boy from Sidikpur who found the head of the yakshi statue and sold it to a stranger from the city.

Orissa.description: A state in eastern India, now officially called Odisha.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India and Feluda's home.

Sidikpur.description: A village near Hasnabad, the site of the plane crash in the story.

Hasnabad.description: A town near Calcutta, referenced as being on the way to Sidikpur.

Archaeological Survey of India.description: A government agency responsible for archaeological research and the protection of cultural heritage in India.

Jessore Road.description: A major road in Kolkata, often used for travel towards the outskirts and neighboring regions.

Barasat.description: A town near Kolkata, mentioned as a landmark on the way to Sidikpur.

VIP Road.description: A prominent road in Kolkata, leading towards the airport and northern suburbs.

Allah.description: The Arabic word for God, used by Muslim villagers in the story.

dhaba.description: A roadside eatery in India, known for serving local food, especially to travelers and truck drivers.

daal.description: A dish made from lentils, commonly eaten in India.

babu.description: A respectful term of address or suffix for a man in India, especially in eastern regions.

hookahs.description: Traditional water pipes used for smoking, common in South Asia.

Mr Mutsuddi.description: The officer-in-charge at Park Street police station, known to Feluda from a previous case.

Mr Adhikari.description: The owner of the flat in Queen’s Mansion and the blue Ambassador, currently away in Darjeeling.

Jayant Mallik.description: Jayant Mallik is a mysterious man staying at the guest house, associated with the blue Ambassador and suspected of involvement in the theft.

Padma Shree.description: A prestigious civilian award in India, given for distinguished contributions in various fields.

Taki.description: A town near Hasnabad, mentioned as the origin of the mysterious man's journey.

Dum Dum.description: A locality in Kolkata, known for its airport and as a major transit point.

Park Street.description: A prominent street in Kolkata, known for its restaurants and colonial-era buildings.

Lowdon Street.description: A street in Kolkata, mentioned as part of the route followed.

Camac Street.description: Another well-known street in Kolkata, referenced in the chase.

Queen’s Mansion.description: A residential building in Kolkata where Mr Mallik is staying.

Waldorf.description: A Chinese restaurant in Kolkata where Feluda and his team have lunch.

Dalhousie Square.description: A historic business district in central Kolkata.

Fairlie Place.description: A location in Kolkata, home to the railway booking office.

Aurangabad.description: A city in Maharashtra, India, to which Mr Mallik books a train ticket.

Sardar Shankar Road.description: A road in Kolkata, where Uncle Sidhu lives and whom Feluda wishes to consult.

Ambassador.description: The Hindustan Ambassador is a classic Indian car model, widely used as taxis and private vehicles in India.

Charminar.description: A popular Indian brand of cigarettes.

OC.description: Abbreviation for Officer-in-Charge, the head of a police station in India.

constable.description: A rank in the Indian police force, typically referring to a lower-level police officer.

Mr Bakshi.description: Feluda's travel agent who assists with booking flights and hotels for the group.

Lalmohan Babu.description: A close friend of Feluda and writer of thriller novels under the pen name Jatayu, who provides comic relief.

Ellora.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site near Aurangabad, famous for its rock-cut caves representing Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain art.

Bombay.description: The former name of Mumbai, a major city in western India.

Baluchistan.description: A region in South Asia, mostly in Pakistan, mentioned as a setting in Lalmohan Babu's story.

Arjun Mehrotra.description: A fictional actor referenced by Lalmohan Babu as a possible fit for his story's hero.

Prakhar Rudra.description: A fictional hero in Lalmohan Babu's new plot.

Sanchi.description: A historical site in Madhya Pradesh, India, known for its ancient Buddhist stupas.

Elephanta.description: Refers to Elephanta Caves, a UNESCO World Heritage site near Mumbai, famous for its rock-cut sculptures.

Simla.description: A hill station in northern India, previously visited by the group.

Dhameeja.description: Refers to a previous case handled by Feluda involving a character named Mr Dhameeja.

Chitpur Road.description: A well-known road in Kolkata, India, referenced for its bumpy rides.

Santa Cruz.description: An area in Mumbai, home to the city's main domestic airport.

Hotel Aurangabad.description: The hotel in Aurangabad where Feluda and his companions stay.

Michigan.description: A state in the USA, mentioned as the workplace of the art history professor.

Vaishnavas.description: Followers of Vaishnavism, a major tradition within Hinduism focusing on the worship of Vishnu.

Hare Krishna.description: A popular name for the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), known for its devotional practices.

Baroda.description: A city in Gujarat, India, known for its educational institutions, including art schools.

Kandaria Mahadev.description: A famous temple in Khajuraho, Madhya Pradesh, renowned for its intricate sculptures.

Khajuraho.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site in Madhya Pradesh, India, known for its group of Hindu and Jain temples.

keertan.description: A devotional singing or chanting, especially in the Hindu tradition.

trunk call.description: A long-distance telephone call, especially one made within India.

air hostess.description: An airline stewardess or flight attendant.

rickety.description: Describes something poorly made and likely to collapse, often used for old vehicles in India.

Shubhankar Bose.description: Shubhankar Bose is a knowledgeable gentleman interested in Indian art, whose disappearance and death are central to the plot.

Malik Ambar.description: An Abyssinian slave who became Prime Minister of Ahmednagar and founded the city that became Aurangabad.

Ahmednagar.description: A historical city and former kingdom in India, associated with Malik Ambar.

Khadke.description: The original name of Aurangabad before it was renamed during Aurangzeb's rule.

Aurangzeb.description: A Mughal emperor of India, after whom Aurangabad was named.

Buddhist caves.description: Ancient rock-cut caves near Aurangabad, known for their statues and carvings.

Bibi ka Makbara.description: A mausoleum in Aurangabad, built in memory of Aurangzeb’s wife, often called the 'second Taj Mahal'.

Ghanashyam Karkat.description: A fictional villain created by Lalmohan Babu for his next book.

Pentax.description: A brand of camera used by Feluda in the story.

paan.description: A preparation combining betel leaf with areca nut and sometimes tobacco, commonly chewed in India.

Marathi.description: An Indian language spoken predominantly in the state of Maharashtra.

sleuth.description: A detective or investigator, often used in reference to amateur detectives in Indian English.

Khuldabad.description: A small town near Ellora, known for its historical significance and proximity to the caves.

City College.description: An educational institution in Calcutta (Kolkata), referenced as part of the characters’ cover story.

City School.description: A school in Calcutta (Kolkata), mentioned as part of the fabricated background for Topshe.

Asia magazine.description: A publication based in Hong Kong, referenced as Feluda’s cover for being a photographer.

Hong Kong.description: A city and special administrative region of China, mentioned as the base of Asia magazine.

Adalat Road.description: A road in Aurangabad, mentioned as a route towards Ellora.

Tourist Guest House.description: A hotel in Khuldabad, described as more expensive and posh compared to the dak bungalow.

Kailash temple.description: The Kailash temple at Ellora is a monumental rock-cut temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, built during the Rashtrakut dynasty in the eighth century.

Raja Krishna.description: A king of the Rashtrakut dynasty, credited with commissioning the Kailash temple.

Rashtrakut dynasty.description: The Rashtrakut dynasty was a powerful Indian dynasty that ruled during the eighth century and built the Kailash temple at Ellora.

Maurya.description: An ancient Indian dynasty, referenced as a historical period.

Sunga.description: An ancient Indian dynasty, referenced as a historical period.

Gupta.description: An ancient Indian dynasty, referenced as a historical period.

Kushan.description: An ancient Indian dynasty, referenced as a historical period.

Chola.description: A South Indian dynasty, referenced as a historical period.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic, referenced as a source of temple carvings.

ganja.description: A Hindi word for marijuana or cannabis, often used in India.

bearer.description: A term used in India for a hotel or household attendant who carries luggage or serves guests.

dak bungalow.description: A colonial-era rest house or guesthouse in India, originally built for government officials.

Mr Raxit.description: R.N. Raxit, whose real name is Chattoraj, is a guest at the bungalow and the main antagonist leading a criminal gang.

Sam Lewison.description: Sam Lewison is an American guest, described as wealthy and the owner of an art gallery in New York.

Rajasthan.description: A state in northwestern India, known for its deserts, palaces, and historical significance.

Stephens Company.description: A company referenced as the maker of a spectacle-case, likely a brand or business based in Calcutta.

New York.description: A major city in the United States, referenced as the location of Sam Lewison's art gallery.

hasnahana.description: A fragrant night-blooming flower, also known as night jasmine or parijat, common in India.

chapati.description: A type of unleavened flatbread, staple in Indian cuisine.

Appa Rao.description: Appa Rao is the fight director of the film crew, who faints upon discovering the dead body.

Rupa.description: Rupa is one of the film's stars, playing the heroine in the movie being shot.

Balwant Chopra.description: Balwant Chopra is a leading actor, playing the villain in the film.

Mohan Sharma.description: Mohan Sharma is the director of the film unit shooting at the temple.

Hindi.description: An official language of India, widely spoken and the primary language of Bollywood films.

bungalow.description: A single-storied house, commonly used in India for residential purposes.

avatar.description: In Hinduism, an incarnation or manifestation of a deity, especially Vishnu.

Mr Kulkarni.description: The manager of the Tourist Guest House, he assists Feluda and provides local information.

Mohanlal.description: The chowkidar (caretaker) of the bungalow, described as trustworthy and long-serving.

chappals.description: Traditional Indian open-toed sandals, usually made of leather.

Mr Ghote.description: Mr Ghote is a police officer or constable in charge of the local police outpost, involved in the investigation and assisting Feluda.

Bengal.description: Bengal refers to a region in eastern India, known for its distinct culture and cuisine.

Das Avatar cave.description: The Das Avatar cave at Ellora is named for its carvings depicting the ten avatars of the Hindu god Vishnu.

kedgeree.description: Kedgeree is a dish of rice, lentils, and fish, popular in Bengal and Anglo-Indian cuisine.

pakoras.description: Pakoras are deep-fried fritters made from vegetables or meat coated in spiced gram flour batter.

hilsa.description: Hilsa is a type of fish highly prized in Bengali cuisine.

Jai Guru.description: Jai Guru is a phrase meaning 'Victory to the Guru' or 'Hail to the teacher', often used as an exclamation or prayer.
